evidence: Brief reads as a real team lead talking: instruction.md:1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.'; :3 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none'; :11 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.'; :13 'Before you hand it over, please check it yourself the way we'll use it' (Colderwater lesson 5 line, in voice). Sentence lengths vary from short ('Conversations are between our side and the candidate.') to long; 7 contractions in the brief. Marketing-gloss grep (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|intuitive|comprehensive|streamline|ensure|utilize|furthermore|moreover|additionally|em dash) returns zero hits across instruction.md, hireops_rules.md and integration.md. No bullet list in instruction.md. hireops_rules.md keeps the same first-person 'we/I' team voice with reasons rather than bare rules (Colderwater lesson 12): :86 'When I move a card I want to see it move straight away.'; :126 "We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands"; :148 'Some conversations run long, so...'; :199 'Candidates are outside the company, so...'; :206 "Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder."; 0 occurrences of 'must', 40 contractions, the plain idiom 'turned down' used for refusals. Its bullet lists (:70-74, :136-140, :164-166) are short permission lists, not polished parallel marketing bullets. integration.md:1-14 is template-controlled text (byte-identical to the template's integration.md) and is impersonal by template design, so it cannot be held against the task; the task-added paragraph :16-19 ('We copy /app as ordinary files when we deploy it, so please don't rely on symbolic links...') matches the brief's voice. Observed only minor, non-defect stiffness: uncontracted 'I am typing'/'I am reading' (instruction.md:5, :7), 'I have not sent' (:7), and instruction.md:15 runtime paragraph is a dense list ('It must start with node /app/server.js, listen on port 3000 ..., expose GET /api/health ..., serve ..., and keep ...') but it is softened by ''How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call'' and ''if that helps'' and carries required runtime facts. Spelling mismatch 'honour'/'honouring' (instruction.md:15) vs template 'honoring' (integration.md:7) is template-controlled and belongs to row 3 if anywhere. Adversarial attempt: looked for an LLM-signature voice (uniform cadence, gloss words, 'ensure that', perfectly parallel headings) or a voice break brief-vs-notes that a portal reviewer could flag; found none beyond the template-owned impersonal integration paragraphs. Whether the rules file mirrors the criteria one-to-one is row 1/5 territory and was not adjudicated here. No runtime measurement is relevant to this row.
